title: Claude Code built-in tool payloads (Claude Code 2.1.309)
$comment: For the input and result of each built-in tool (definitions <Tool>Input and <Tool>Result). Generated from Claude Code 2.1.309 by calling the zod v4 toJSONSchema embedded in the binary on its own validator (method A, runtime export). Anchor: the tool factory that copies a tool definition's properties (getters included), read as inputSchema and outputSchema on each tool. Do not edit by hand: run "bun run schemas".

Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

staying.description: How many entries stay on the machine and are counted here.

stays.description: The entries that stay and are named, each with why.

list.description: The list, a line each, of every file sent and every entry that stays and is named, and a last line saying so where entries stay unnamed: its sha256, and the file that holds it.

unnamed.description: Present only when the lists are over the bound: how many files and entries they do not name. The list file names them.

message.description: The notification body. Keep it under 200 characters; mobile OSes truncate.

sentAt.description: ISO timestamp captured at tool execution on the emitting process. Optional — resumed sessions replay pre-sentAt outputs verbatim.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

uri.description: The directory resource URI to list

resources.description: Direct children of the directory resource. Subdirectories appear with mimeType "inode/directory".

error.description: Human-readable error when the server could not list the directory

blobSavedTo.description: Path where binary blob content was saved

error.description: Human-readable error when the server could not read the resource

notification_id.description: Server-assigned stable id — the dedup key across redeliveries.

origin.description: Server-attested source token: "github_webhook" | "trigger_fire" | "mcp_send_message" (open set; unknown well-formed tokens pass through verbatim, off-grammar values coerce to "unknown").

queued_at.description: RFC3339 timestamp of when the backend queued it.

arrived_at.description: RFC3339 timestamp, by this machine's clock, of when the notification reached this session's queue. Missing from results saved before this field existed.

remaining.description: Notifications still queued after this drain (drains are size-budgeted); call the tool again to read them.

read_at.description: RFC3339 timestamp, by this machine's clock, of when this call read the queue. Missing from results saved before this field existed.

filePath.description: The path to the file that was read

numLines.description: Number of lines in the returned content

totalLines.description: Total number of lines in the file

truncatedByTokenCap.description: True when a whole-file read was auto-paginated because it exceeded the token cap (the content is a partial first page). A programmatic signal for internal consumers; survives output reconstruction (unlike the render-time banner).

artifactRead.description: Set when this Read completed a saved Artifact source file: the Artifact and the version of it that now counts as viewed.

type.description: The MIME type of the image

dimensions.description: Image dimension info for coordinate mapping

displayWidth.description: Displayed image width in pixels (after resizing)

displayHeight.description: Displayed image height in pixels (after resizing)

filePath.description: The path to the notebook file
The path to the PDF file
The path to the PDF file

firstPage.description: Document page number of the first extracted page (1 when no range was requested); labels the page images in the model-facing tool_result

totalPages.description: @internal Number of pages in the document. Set only when the call named no page range and the PDF was too long to read whole, so only its first pages were extracted

pages.description: Extracted page images, in page order. Present only transiently in-process: the page image bytes are delivered solely as image blocks in the model-facing tool_result content and are not retained on the tool_use_result, so this key is absent on the emitted/persisted result

base64.description: Base64-encoded page image; empty when the page could not be processed

mediaType.description: The MIME type of the image

error.description: Why the page could not be processed as an image; set only when base64 is empty

source.description: Set when the dedup matched a startup-seeded entry (CLAUDE.md / nested memory) rather than a prior Read tool_result

server.description: Optional server name: refresh only this server. Omit to refresh all connected servers.

status.description: refreshed: tool list re-queried and applied. error: the re-query failed and the previous tool set was kept. not_connected: the server has no live connection to query (this tool never dials).

toolCount.description: Number of tools now available from this server

error.description: Why the refresh failed or the server was unavailable

trigger_id.description: Required for get, update, run, and list_runs

session_id.description: Required for get_run_log: a run session id (cse_… or session_…, from list_runs)

cursor.description: next_cursor from a previous list_runs or get_run_log page

body.description: Required for create and update; optional for run

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

scheduledFor.description: Epoch ms timestamp when the next wakeup will fire

clampedDelaySeconds.description: Actual delay used after clamping to runtime bounds

wasClamped.description: True if the requested delaySeconds was outside [60, 3600]

stopped.description: True when the model ended the loop via `stop: true`

cancelledWakeups.description: How many pending dynamic-loop wakeups stop:true cancelled. 0 means nothing was pending — a recurring /loop cron is not cancelled by stop:true.

keywords.description: Keyword phrases describing the user's intent or a named product.
Keyword phrases describing the user's intent.
Keyword phrases describing the user's intent.

type.description: What kind of feedback this is.

title.description: Short, specific one-line summary of the issue.

details.description: Labeled bullets, in order: **What happened:** (observed vs. expected, exact error text if short); **What the user said:** (quoted, or "User didn't comment; observed by the model."); **Repro:** (minimal steps); **Evidence:** (request IDs, timestamps, paths, versions; omit if none); optionally a final **Cause:** only if verified in-session. One to three lines per bullet. No narrative paragraphs, no speculation, no secrets.

area.description: Optional short tag naming the part of Claude Code this is about (e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing"). Leave blank if unclear.

failure_mode.description: When the report is about MODEL BEHAVIOR (not a product bug), the closest failure mode, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value. Omit only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.

task_category.description: What kind of task the session was doing when the issue occurred, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.

to.description: Recipient: a peer session name from ListAgents, or an explicit uds:<socket> / bridge:<session id> address

files.description: File paths (absolute or relative to cwd) to send. Always pass an array, even for a single file.

message.description: Optional short message delivered alongside the files

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

files.description: File paths (absolute or relative to cwd) to send to the user. Always pass an array, even for a single file.

caption.description: Optional short caption for the file(s).

status.description: Use 'proactive' when you're surfacing a file the user hasn't asked for and needs to see now — a generated artifact, a completed report. Use 'normal' when replying to something the user just said.

display.description: How the client should present the file. 'render' opens it inline in the side panel (for HTML, SVG, Mermaid, images, PDFs — anything the user wants to look at now). 'attach' shows a download card only, no inline preview (for deliverables the user will save and open elsewhere). Omit to let the client decide by file type — today that means renderable types render and everything else attaches, same as before this parameter existed.

message.description: The message for the user. Supports markdown formatting.

sentAt.description: ISO timestamp captured at tool execution on the emitting process. Optional — resumed sessions replay pre-sentAt outputs verbatim.

mode.description: 'check' (default): if ONBOARDING.md is present locally, uploads it to the most-recent guide (creates one if none exist); otherwise reports the existing link without uploading. 'update': upload to a specific guide by short_code. 'create': always make a new link. 'delete': remove a guide.

short_code.description: Short code of a specific guide to target (returned by a previous call). Honored by check, update, and delete — skips the org-wide lookup and targets this guide directly.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

model.description: Resolved model the skill turn runs on when a frontmatter model override took effect; omitted otherwise

readOnly.description: True when the skill instructions were loaded read-only (nothing was executed)

agentId.description: The ID of the sub-agent that executed the skill

result.description: The result from the forked skill execution

background.description: True when the sub-agent was launched in the background: `result` describes the launch, and the skill outcome arrives later as a task notification.

message.description: Your full report for your caller

uuids.description: directoryUuid or server_id values to resolve.

contextLabel.description: Short header tying the suggestion to the user request.

keywords.description: Topic keywords from the user's request.

subject.description: A brief title for the task

activeForm.description: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")

metadata.description: Arbitrary metadata to attach to the task

taskId.description: The ID of the task to retrieve

task_id.description: The ID of the background task to stop. Agent-team teammates and named background agents are also accepted by agent ID or name.
The ID of the task that was stopped

task_type.description: The type of the task that was stopped

command.description: The command or description of the stopped task

taskId.description: The ID of the task to update

activeForm.description: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")

addBlocks.description: Task IDs that this task blocks

addBlockedBy.description: Task IDs that block this task

metadata.description: Metadata keys to merge into the task. Set a key to null to delete it.

oldTodos.description: The todo list before the update

newTodos.description: The todo list after the update

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

servers.description: Server names to wait for (default: all pending)

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

offset.description: Character position in the page text to start reading from. Use it to read on through a page too long for one call, with the value the previous result gave.

bytes.description: Size of the fetched content in bytes

result.description: Processed result from applying the prompt to the content

durationMs.description: Time taken to fetch and process the content

allowed_domains.description: Only include search results from these domains

blocked_domains.description: Never include search results from these domains

query.description: The search query that was executed

title.description: The title of the search result

url.description: The URL of the search result

snippet.description: Page text. PostToolUse hooks get it; tool_use_result does not.

results.description: Search results and/or text commentary from the model

durationSeconds.description: Time taken to complete the search operation

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

taskType.description: TaskType of the registered background task — 'local_workflow' for in-process runs, 'remote_agent' when remote:true dispatches to CCR. Set on all new writes; absent only on transcripts written before this field existed.

workflowName.description: meta.name from the workflow script — same value as task_started.workflow_name. Set on all new writes; absent only on transcripts written before this field existed.

runId.description: Local workflow run identifier for resumeFromRunId. Absent for remote_launched (the CCR session URL is the resume handle there) and on transcripts written before this field existed.

transcriptDir.description: Directory where subagent transcripts are written during execution

scriptPath.description: Path to the persisted workflow script for this invocation. Editable via Write/Edit; pass back as `scriptPath` to re-run without resending the script.

sessionUrl.description: CCR session URL when status is remote_launched

warning.description: Non-blocking heads-up (e.g. local git state diverges from the pushed branch the cloud session will clone)

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

type.description: Whether a new file was created or an existing file was updated

filePath.description: The path to the file that was written

content.description: The content that was written to the file

structuredPatch.description: Diff patch showing the changes (empty when nothing changed, the diff timed out, or — with originalFile null on an update — the previous content was too large to diff)

originalFile.description: The original file content before the write (null for new files, or when the previous content was too large to include)

userModified.description: True when the user edited the proposed content in the permission dialog before accepting

staged.description: True when the write was held for the machine owner to review instead of written; the file is unchanged

store.description: Id of the memory store to list. Omit to list the memory stores available in this session (id, description, writable or read-only, and the path of its index document).

path_prefix.description: Optional directory prefix to list only documents under it (e.g. /feedback/). Matching is directory-aligned (/x is the same as /x/). Omit to list the whole store.

cursor.description: Path of the last entry from a previous call. Returns entries after this path.

store.description: Id of the memory store to read from (call memory_list with no arguments to see the stores available in this session).

path.description: Path of the memory document to read (e.g. /MEMORY.md).

store.description: Id of the memory store to write to (call memory_list with no arguments to see the stores available in this session).

path.description: Path of the document to create or update (e.g. /feedback_testing.md).

content.description: Full text content to write (UTF-8). Replaces the entire document — any line you omit is deleted. Line endings are normalized to LF, invisible/format characters are stripped, and other control characters are replaced with U+FFFD. Empty or whitespace-only content is rejected. Capped at 100KB per document.

if_version.description: Pass the 12-character version token from your most recent memory_read or memory_write of this file. For a file that does not yet exist (not shown in the listing), pass the literal word new (without quotes; an empty string is treated the same way). For any file already in the listing, memory_read it first to get its version token — the listing itself does not contain version tokens. Never invent a value.

name.description: kebab-case skill slug; must not contain "claude" or "anthropic"; at most 64 characters for a new skill

target.description: Name of the existing skill to update. Required when kind is 'improvement'; omit for 'new'.

description.description: One short sentence saying when to use this skill: aim for under 200 characters, never more than 1024, and no angle brackets. Shown on the review card and saved as the skill's description, which is what decides when the skill is used. For an improvement, reuse the existing skill's description unless the change alters when the skill applies.

evidence.description: memory file paths where this procedure was observed

skillMd.description: The complete SKILL.md exactly as it should be saved: frontmatter plus the full body. When the user saves, the body below the frontmatter becomes the skill's entire instructions and the name and description come from the fields above; other frontmatter keys are not kept. For an improvement this replaces the existing skill's SKILL.md entirely, so read that skill's current SKILL.md first and include everything worth keeping, not only the changes.

proposalCount.description: Number of proposals shown on the review card

runner_id.description: Tagged runner id (ccrunner_…) the caller observed failing. Server verifies this still matches the session assignment; mismatch returns Conflict. For a stuck session whose runner is gone, any value is accepted.

secret_file_path.description: Path to the environment secret the operator saved from the Admin UI.

base_dir.description: Always passed to the runner (its built-in default of /workspace is unwritable on laptops). Default: ./runner-setup/workspace

bytes.description: How many trailing bytes to read. Default 65536.
